newsitem.title: USA: N.J. $3 bln bond plan wins key endorsement - paper.
newsitem.headline: N.J. $3 bln bond plan wins key endorsement - paper.

text.p: New Jersey Gov. Christine Whitman's plan to sell $2.9 billion of taxable pension obligation bonds has won support from the state's powerful teachers union, the Star Ledger reported Friday.

The 150,000 New Jersey Education Association, which two years ago sued the Whitman Administration over its handling of teacher pensions, said it would withdraw that lawsuit and put its full backing behind Whitman's latest pension plan.
The proposal, which still needs legislative approval, involves selling $2.9 billion of taxable bonds to help fully fund the pension system's $4.2 billion unfunded liability.

At the same time, the state will use a large portion of the fund's surplus to free up $647 million in one-time savings for the fiscal 1997 and 1998 budgets, enabling Whitman to avoid harsh spending cuts to balance the budget.
The union said it would embark on a letter writing campaign in support of the bond plan, which it said will place the pension system on a sound footing.
Opponents of the bond sale say it would eliminate financial flexibility by replacing the "soft" liability of unfunded pensions with a "hard" liability of debt service on bonds.
